title: Rigidity of natural compact-support transformations
statement: Let l be a prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, and k any field in which l is invertible. Let X,Y be finite-type k-schemes and f:X→Y a separated finite-type k-morphism with compactification c. Consider two natural transformations tau,tau' from the actual completed proper/open compact-support functor restricted to integral constructible inputs [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] into the recorded integral compact-support functor followed by ambient inclusion [def-weil-compact-support-finite-action]. If at every integral constructible input and every positive finite coefficient exponent the images of their components under actual derived scalar reduction are equal, then tau=tau'. This is a statement about natural transformations between these specified functors, not arbitrary individual morphisms in a derived category.

source.place: Proof of sk-prop-scalar-six-compact-support; Bhatt--Scholze 6.7.6, 6.7.7 and 6.1.13; Stacks 0941 and 0F7J

proof.text: It suffices to compare the transformations on constructible integral inputs in the essential image of finite scalar restriction. This is torsion-input detection, an adic density assertion about natural transformations.
For an input in the essential image of restriction at level n, its recorded compact-support value is also in that essential image, at the same level.

For any adjunction L adjoint to R, L detects equality of maps into an object isomorphic to R(N): conjugate the target to R(N), and apply the inverse Hom equivalence f mapping to L(f) followed by the counit at N. Equal L-images have equal inverse transposes, hence are equal. Apply this to the actual finite scalar-extension/restriction adjunction and the assumed nth reduction equality. The preceding steps then give equality of the natural transformations.

proof_origin.place: Torsion-input detection, preservation of its finite quotient coefficient action, and the finite scalar-adjunction Hom equivalence; refinement of the original rigidity plan.
